requirements.label: Admin power is not a bare key
A confirmed delay before changes apply, no bypass
Bypass paths of the delay checked and ruled out
Price feed not under one hand
No key shared with another tracked protocol

exit_window: none: a change applies at once

narrative.summary: One plain HyperCore key leads HLP and its 7 child strategy vaults, about $186M of account value in total. It has trading and allocation power but cannot withdraw funds to itself, and depositors face a 4-day lock.
narrative.detail: The leader key reads as a single key on HyperCore (no multisig, no EVM code) and has 6 named API wallets. Its power is trading, capital allocation and backstop liquidations, not custody, and leaderCommission is 0. It is still scored on the standard single-key ladder, because a compromised key could destroy value through bad-faith trading, and the 4-day deposit lock (per Hyperliquid docs) means depositors cannot exit ahead of a developing episode. No separate vault-leader formula was invented; the difference from custody targets is disclosed instead.

reproduce.note: this RPC cannot replay the block of the build (it ignores the block tag, or no longer serves old state): the call reproduces the current value, not the one of the build; compare the composite and lastUpdated with this page

cheapest_fix.what: a stronger admin setup (admin power spread beyond one key, or checked by others)

main_gap.requirement: Admin power is not a bare key
main_gap.reason: One key, or a tiny group, can change it

independent_read.why: no code at this address on the chain's mainnet: a derived identifier for a native (non-EVM) entity such as HyperCore, or a contract that lives on another chain (a rollup's own L1 contracts); nothing for this reader to compare here
